faq.q: How does Verdure recognize my plants without a connection?
faq.a: A recognition model is built into the app. When you take or choose a photo, it is analyzed right on your iPhone or iPad: nothing is sent over the internet, and it all works even in airplane mode. When Verdure is unsure, it offers several choices instead of confidently guessing wrong.

faq.q: Verdure doesn't recognize my plant, what can I do?
faq.a: Take the photo in bright light, with a leaf or flower clearly visible against a simple background, and try again. Recognition covers about 240 houseplants and balcony plants: if yours isn't one of them, search for it by name in the Explore tab, which holds 282 care sheets.

faq.q: My watering reminders don't arrive, why?
faq.a: First check that notifications are allowed: Settings › Notifications › Verdure, then turn on "Allow Notifications". Also make sure a Focus mode or Do Not Disturb isn't active at the reminder time. Verdure sends a single reminder a day, at the time you choose in its Settings, with all of the day's care. Reminders are scheduled on your device, with no server.

faq.q: What does Verdure+ include and how much does it cost?
faq.a: The free version gives you 3 recognitions a month, 2 tracked plants with their watering reminders, all the care sheets, and in the vegetable garden the calendar, the vegetable sheets and one bed. Verdure+ costs €4.99 a month, with a 7-day free trial: unlimited recognitions and plants, the plant doctor, fertilizing, repotting and misting reminders, the photo journal, and in the garden unlimited beds, crop rotation and sowing and harvest reminders.

faq.q: How do I cancel or restore my subscription?
faq.a: The subscription is sold and managed by Apple. To cancel, open Settings › your name › Subscriptions › Verdure, at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. On a new device, tap "Restore Purchases" in Verdure's Settings to get back a subscription you already paid for.

It is indicative only, based on public sources (notably the ASPCA for cats and dogs). It does not replace medical or veterinary advice. If your pet or a child has eaten a plant, call your vet or a poison control center right away.

faq.q: Where do the photos on the care sheets come from?
faq.a: The reference photos come from iNaturalist and Wikimedia Commons under free licenses and are bundled in the app. The author and license of each photo are listed in Settings › Photo credits.

faq.q: Where are my plants and photos stored?
faq.a: Only on your device, in Verdure's private storage. There is no account and no server. Removing a plant erases its data; deleting the app erases everything. They may be included in your device's iCloud or iTunes backups, which you manage in Apple's settings.

support.privacy_summary: Verdure collects no data, asks for no account and contains no ads or trackers. Plant recognition happens on your device: your photos are never sent anywhere.

blocks.p: Verdure collects no data. Everything you do in the app stays on your iPhone or iPad.

ul: No account, no ads, no tracking: Verdure includes no analytics or advertising tools and does not identify you in any way.

blocks.p: Photos you take or choose are analyzed by a model installed in the app, without any connection. They are not sent anywhere.
The camera is only used to frame a plant inside the app. The photo library is only read for photos you pick yourself (recognition, photo journal). Nothing is read in the background.

They are stored in the app's private storage on your device. Removing a plant or deleting the app erases them. They may be included in your device's iCloud or iTunes backups, which you manage yourself in Apple's settings.
Watering and care reminders are scheduled on the device; no server is involved.

The Verdure+ subscription is sold and managed by Apple. Verdure sees neither your payment method nor your identity; the app only checks through the App Store whether a subscription is active, to unlock features.
The photos on care sheets come from iNaturalist and Wikimedia Commons (free licenses) and are bundled in the app; credits are in Settings › Photo credits.
Verdure collects no data, including from children.
